I show that this scheme yields improved concentration bounds on the gradient variance under mild ergodicity assumptions. Lastly, I emphasize that adjoint methods for SDEs offer a general-purpose theoretical framework for gradient-based learning in continuous-time latent variable models. This formulation unifies variational inference, score-based learning, and control-theoretic perspectives on optimization. By modeling the learning dynamics as a coupled forward-backward SDE system, I introduce a new analytical paradigm for reasoning about parameter updates and convergence properties in stochastic generative models. My model architecture is designed to facilitate scalable learning in continuous-time stochastic systems while maintaining modularity and interpretability. The encoder is implemented as a bidirectional recurrent neural network (RNN), such as a Bi-GRU or Transformer encoder, which processes the full observation sequence 𝐱 1 : T \mathbf{x}_{1:T} and outputs the parameters of a variational distribution q ϕ ​ ( z 0 | 𝐱 1 : T ) q_{\phi}(z_{0}|\mathbf{x}_{1:T}) . This amortized inference scheme allows us to initialize latent trajectories with strong temporal context, serving as the basis for subsequent SDE-based evolution.
